No predecessor PR is attributed. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Needs maintainer review before merge - 5 items remain** Keep open: the PR repairs a real current-main regression but introduces two P1 policy leaks that can activate unlisted meeting tools or evaluate compatibility state from the wrong environment. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `7f926d25cd8aca765f7d4768e5ba0c8598dd2742` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The PR has credible real-path evidence for the original regression but needs two bounded policy corrections before it is merge-ready. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): The captured PR body ties the changed activation owner to an isolated Doctor migration, source Gateway startup, and plugins.list comparison on the exact head, with strict-mode and explicit-deny controls; it sufficiently proves the central repair but not the identified regressions. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 2 actionable review findings remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): The captured PR body ties the changed activation owner to an isolated Doctor migration, source Gateway startup, and plugins.list comparison on the exact head, with strict-mode and explicit-deny controls; it sufficiently proves the central repair but not the identified regressions. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 7 items | Current main still has the regression: Current main uses generic activation for runtime providers and does not apply the PR's bundled-provider compatibility transform.
Introduced tool activation widening: The new provider-compat predicate treats any bundled transcript-source owner as eligible; index construction then applies the compatibility transform to it.
Bundled meeting plugins contradict the provider-only boundary: Google Meet, Zoom Meetings, and Teams Meetings are default-enabled command/tool plugins whose only matching compatibility contract is transcriptSourceProviders. | | **Findings** | 2 actionable findings | [P1] Restrict compatibility to actual provider owners
[P1] Forward the scoped environment through enablement rechecks | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Doctor stores legacy bundled-discovery mode in SQLite; plugin discovery, the installed index, Gateway startup, and provider loading use it to decide which plugins activate. The compatibility path must preserve provider defaults without widening channel, tool, or command activation. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Legacy plugin configuration] --> B[Doctor migration] B --> C[SQLite compatibility state] C --> D[Plugin activation policy] D --> E[Installed plugin index] E --> F[Gateway startup] E --> G[Provider loading] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Restrict compatibility to actual provider owners (P1)** - `transcriptSourceProviders` also marks Google Meet, Zoom Meetings, and Teams Meetings—default-enabled tool/command plugins—as compatibility providers. The index then adds their IDs to `plugins.allow`, so they activate despite being omitted. This was visible on the prior reviewed head and was missed; exclude mixed tool/command owners and add a restrictive-allowlist regression. - [ ] **Forward the scoped environment through enablement rechecks (P1)** - The new compatibility branch consults its optional `env`, but explicit-environment consumers such as setup backend lookup, plugin inspection, and provider-auth evidence omit it after building metadata with that same env. They fall back to `process.env` and can report a compat-enabled bundled provider as disabled; propagate the resolved environment and cover two roots. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Under a restrictive allowlist, default-enabled Google Meet, Zoom Meetings, and Teams Meetings can become enabled because their transcript-source contract is treated as provider eligibility. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Explicit-environment setup, inspection, registry, and provider-auth paths can re-evaluate a correctly scoped index against process.env and hide compatibility-enabled providers. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Production code grows by 234 net lines for a bug fix; the repair should consolidate the compatibility classification and state-root propagation at their canonical owners. ## Findings - [P1] Restrict compatibility to actual provider owners — `src/plugins/bundled-provider-compat.ts:38-40` - [P1] Forward the scoped environment through enablement rechecks — `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.ts:182-193`

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Root-cause cluster Relationship: `fixed_by_candidate` Canonical: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123297 Summary: This PR is the candidate repair for the linked bundled-discovery allowlist regression, but it remains incomplete. Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123297 - The linked issue describes the same migrated allowlist compatibility failure that the PR targets. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Repair the compatibility boundary (recommended)** Exclude mixed transcript/tool plugins from provider compatibility and forward the resolved environment through all enablement rechecks before merge.

### Technical review Best possible solution: Restrict compatibility to actual provider owners, preserve strict activation for mixed tool/command plugins, and thread the resolved environment through every dynamic enablement recheck with two-root regression coverage. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes: current source deterministically adds each qualifying plugin to the allowlist, and activation then enables bundled default plugins; the captured isolated Gateway comparison corroborates the central regression. Is this the best way to solve the issue? No: classifying every transcript-source contract as a provider owner violates the PR's stated provider-only boundary, and optional environment propagation cannot preserve scoped machine-state semantics. Full review comments: - [P1] Restrict compatibility to actual provider owners — `src/plugins/bundled-provider-compat.ts:38-40` `transcriptSourceProviders` also marks Google Meet, Zoom Meetings, and Teams Meetings—default-enabled tool/command plugins—as compatibility providers. The index then adds their IDs to `plugins.allow`, so they activate despite being omitted. This was visible on the prior reviewed head and was missed; exclude mixed tool/command owners and add a restrictive-allowlist regression. Confidence: 0.99 Late finding: first raised on code an earlier review cycle already covered. - [P1] Forward the scoped environment through enablement rechecks — `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.ts:182-193` The new compatibility branch consults its optional `env`, but explicit-environment consumers such as setup backend lookup, plugin inspection, and provider-auth evidence omit it after building metadata with that same env. They fall back to `process.env` and can report a compat-enabled bundled provider as disabled; propagate the resolved environment and cover two roots. Confidence: 0.97 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.98 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Sufficient (live_output): The captured PR body ties the changed activation owner to an isolated Doctor migration, source Gateway startup, and plugins.list comparison on the exact head, with strict-mode and explicit-deny controls; it sufficiently proves the central repair but not the identified regressions. - `proof: sufficient`: Contributor real behavior proof is sufficient. The captured PR body ties the changed activation owner to an isolated Doctor migration, source Gateway startup, and plugins.list comparison on the exact head, with strict-mode and explicit-deny controls; it sufficiently proves the central repair but not the identified regressions. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - [P1] pnpm test src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.compat.test.ts. - [P1] pnpm test src/plugins/manifest-contract-eligibility.test.ts. - [P1] pnpm test src/plugins/capability-provider-runtime.test.ts. - [P1] pnpm check:changed -- src/plugins/bundled-provider-compat.ts src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.ts src/plugins/setup-registry.runtime.ts src/plugins/management-service.ts src/secrets/provider-env-vars.ts. What I checked: - **Current main still has the regression:** Current main uses generic activation for runtime providers and does not apply the PR's bundled-provider compatibility transform. ([`src/plugins/providers.runtime.ts:248`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ee3ee255d8d9/src/plugins/providers.runtime.ts#L248), [ee3ee255d8d9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ee3ee255d8d9)) - **Introduced tool activation widening:** The new provider-compat predicate treats any bundled transcript-source owner as eligible; index construction then applies the compatibility transform to it. ([`src/plugins/bundled-provider-compat.ts:38`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f926d25cd8a/src/plugins/bundled-provider-compat.ts#L38), [7f926d25cd8a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7f926d25cd8a)) - **Bundled meeting plugins contradict the provider-only boundary:** Google Meet, Zoom Meetings, and Teams Meetings are default-enabled command/tool plugins whose only matching compatibility contract is transcriptSourceProviders. ([`extensions/google-meet/openclaw.plugin.json:16`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ee3ee255d8d9/extensions/google-meet/openclaw.plugin.json#L16), [ee3ee255d8d9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ee3ee255d8d9)) - **Allowlist result enables the widened plugin set:** After the transform adds an ID to plugins.allow, activation passes the allowlist and enables a default-enabled bundled plugin. ([`src/plugins/config-activation-shared.ts:196`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f926d25cd8a/src/plugins/config-activation-shared.ts#L196), [7f926d25cd8a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7f926d25cd8a)) - **Scoped environment is dropped by existing enablement consumers:** The introduced recheck accepts env, but setup and plugin inspection build metadata with an explicit env then omit it when re-evaluating enabled state. ([`src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.ts:182`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7f926d25cd8a/src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.ts#L182), [7f926d25cd8a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7f926d25cd8a)) - **Submitted real-path proof:** The captured PR body records isolated Doctor migration, source Gateway startup, and plugins.list results for exact head 7f926d25, including strict and explicit-deny controls; it does not cover the two newly identified leaks. ([7f926d25cd8a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7f926d25cd8a)) Likely related people: - **Peter Steinberger:** Suggested for follow-up; no historical authorship or introduction is verified.
